Now I understand the issue clearly. In `updateTask`, when updating a task, the code does:

```ts
const updated: Task = {
  ...existing,
  title: updates.title as any,
  description: updates.description as any,
  priority: updates.priority as any,
  status: updates.status as any,
  dueDate: updates.dueDate as any,
  updatedAt: toISOTimestamp(new Date()),
};
```

The problem is that if `updates.title` is `undefined`, it will overwrite `existing.title` with `undefined`. In JavaScript, when you spread an object and explicitly set a key to `undefined`, it becomes `undefined` (unlike in JSON serialization where `undefined` is omitted).

The fix is to only set fields that are actually provided (not `undefined`). Let me write a reproduction script first.
